questions.questionText: Explain how supply-side policies can help to achieve a low, stable rate of inflation.
Which one of the following statements about supply-side policies is correct? Supply-side policies
options: have no effect on aggregate demand.
often rely on creating economic incentives.
only affect long-run aggregate supply.
usually lead to an increase in inflation.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is a supply-side policy that is most likely to lead to an improvement in the balance of trade in goods and services on the current account of the UK’s balance of payments?
options: A significant and sustained reduction in Bank Rate by the Monetary Policy Committee of the Bank of England
Deregulation that makes it easier for UK transnational corporations to invest abroad
Increasing the supply of pounds on the foreign exchange market to reduce the exchange rate and make exports cheaper
Tax breaks for manufacturing firms that invest in upgrading their machinery and other capital goods

questions.questionText: After considering Extract D, and the original evidence in Extracts A, B and C, would you recommend that the Government continue to subsidise firms to encourage them to set up gigafactories to produce batteries in the UK? Justify your recommendation.

Extract E (lines 17–18) states: ‘A low rate of corporation tax has also contributed to both short-run and long-run economic growth.’ With the help of a diagram, explain how a low rate of corporation tax may cause short-run and long-run economic growth.
Which one of the following is most likely to bring about a supply-side improvement in an economy? A fall in
options: company profits
incentives for enterprise
income tax rates
labour productivity

questions.questionText: A government introduces a number of supply-side policies that increase the size of the country's working population and labour productivity. All other things being equal, which one of the following statements identifies the most likely effects of the policies on the country's economy?
options: An increase in real national income and a reduction in the balance of payments deficit
An increase in short-run economic growth and inflation
An increase in the trend rate of economic growth and a growing balance of payments deficit
A reduction in unemployment and an increase in inflation

questions.questionText: Explain why investment in infrastructure in the less-prosperous regions could help to improve the prosperity of people living in these regions.

After considering Extract D, and the original evidence in Extracts A, B and C, would you recommend that the government intervene in the economy to try to reduce the differences in the economic prosperity of the various regions of the United Kingdom? Justify your recommendation.

An economy has a low rate of economic growth and high unemployment. Which one of the following sets of policies would be most likely to increase growth and reduce unemployment whilst avoiding a rise in inflation?
options: A cut in income tax and lower interest rates
Higher interest rates and an appreciation in the exchange rate
Higher welfare benefits and an increase in the money supply
Increased expenditure on training and an investment subsidy

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is most likely to be an instrument of industrial policy?
options: An increase in manufacturing productivity
Government grants for firms with growth potential
Higher investment by firms in research and development
Investment by firms in artificial intelligence

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is an example of a contractionary fiscal policy designed to reduce inflation while, at the same time, minimising the negative impact on the economy’s potential for long-run economic growth?
options: A decrease in the budget deficit and replacement of a sugar tax with a tax on savings
An increase in interest rates and replacement of food subsidies with subsidies for innovation
An increase in the budget surplus and a switch from spending on pensions to spending on new airports
Restrictions on bank lending and a switch from spending on arts degrees to spending on apprenticeships

questions.questionText: Figure 8 shows the aggregate demand curve (AD) and the long-run aggregate supply curves (LRAS) for an economy. A redistribution of government spending from spending on welfare towards the funding of research and development shifts the long-run aggregate supply curve from LRAS1 to LRAS2. Which one of the following is the most likely effect of this policy?
options: A decrease in the number of people who are economically active
An improvement in the balance of payments on current account
An increase in the size of the government’s budget deficit
The creation of a positive output gap

questions.questionText: Evaluate the view that supply-side improvements in the UK economy can best be achieved through the use of interventionist policies.
A government cuts the rate of corporation tax from 30% to 15%. This policy is most likely intended to
options: decrease the level of savings.
improve labour mobility.
reduce investment from overseas companies.
stimulate supply-side improvements.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is a supply-side policy aimed at reducing the natural rate of unemployment?
options: Government retraining schemes for structurally unemployed workers
Increasing legal protection against unfair dismissal for employees
Increasing the real value of the national minimum wage
New government subsidies for developers of artificial intelligence

questions.questionText: After considering Extract D, and the original evidence in Extracts A, B and C, would you recommend that the UK government provides financial and other support to companies involved in the production of commercial aircraft? Justify your recommendation.
Which one of the following statements regarding supply-side policies is correct? Supply-side policies
options: can have microeconomic as well as macroeconomic effects on the economy.
can increase the potential output of an economy but not its trend rate of growth.
cannot be used to correct market failures and improve the operation of markets.
do not affect competitiveness or the current account of the balance of payments.

questions.questionText: Extract B (lines 13–14) states: ‘It can be argued that supply-side reforms have gone too far in creating a highly flexible workforce and the government needs to do more in terms of protecting the nation’s workers’. Using the data in the extracts and your knowledge of economics, evaluate the view that free market supply-side reforms to labour markets are beneficial to the UK economy.

An economy has recently recovered from a recession and closed its negative output gap. The government would now like to increase the trend rate of economic growth. Which one of the following policies is likely to be the most effective?
options: Expansionary fiscal policy
Expansionary monetary policy
Redistributive policies
Supply-side policies

questions.questionText: Figure 5 shows the aggregate demand (AD) and long-run aggregate supply (LRAS) curves for an economy. Which one of the following policies is most likely to have caused aggregate demand to shift from AD1 to AD2, and long-run aggregate supply to shift from LRAS1 to LRAS2?
options: A lower rate of corporation tax
A reduction in the money supply
An increase in state pensions
An increase in the exchange rate

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements about supply-side policies and supply-side improvements is true?
options: Supply-side improvements do not affect the balance of payments on current account
Supply-side improvements often originate in the private sector
Supply-side policies have no impact on the budget balance
Supply-side policies work by leaving incentives unchanged

questions.questionText: In the diagram below, as a result of the government implementing a new industrial policy, the long-run aggregate supply curve shifts from LRAS1 to LRAS2 The shift in LRAS suggests that the industrial policy is most likely to have
options: caused firms to be more innovative.
created a positive output gap.
reduced employment and inflation.
reduced imports and exports.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following policies is most likely to improve the supply side of the economy? A policy which
options: increases the budget surplus.
reduces the natural rate of unemployment.
shifts resources from capital to labour intensive industries.
shifts the burden of tax from indirect to direct taxation.

questions.questionText: The diagram below shows the aggregate demand (AD) curve, the short-run aggregate supply (SRAS) curve and the long-run aggregate supply (LRAS) curve for an economy. The economy’s initial equilibrium is at E1. The government wants to achieve economic growth without conflicting with its long-run objective of price stability. All other things being equal, which one of the following policy combinations is most likely to enable the economy to achieve a new long-run equilibrium at E2?
options: A reduction in interest rates and increased government borrowing.
A reduction in the budget deficit and the rate of growth of the money supply.
Increased government expenditure on apprenticeships and transport infrastructure funded through borrowing.
Increased government expenditure on welfare funded through higher indirect taxes.

questions.questionText: A government wants to increase the economy’s rate of long-run economic growth by implementing a supply-side policy. Which one of the following is a government policy aimed at stimulating the supply side of the economy?
options: A new scheme to help young people buy their own homes
Greater provision of care homes for the elderly
Measures to promote competition between businesses
More generous welfare benefits for unemployed workers

questions.questionText: Explain how fiscal policy can be used to try to improve the supply side of an economy.
Explain how government policies can reduce the natural rate of unemployment.
Which one of the following is most likely to improve the supply-side performance of an economy? An increase in
options: government spending on welfare benefits.
growth in the rest of the world.
labour productivity.
the basic rate of income tax.

questions.questionText: Taking into account Extract D, and the original evidence presented in Extracts A, B and C, would you recommend that the government should intervene to support the UK steel industry? Justify your recommendation.

A country has a slow rate of growth of productivity and rising cyclical unemployment. All other things being equal, which measures are most likely to increase the rate of growth of productivity and reduce cyclical unemployment?
options: Increased investment and increased saving
More government spending on training and a higher exchange rate
Decreased benefit payments and a lower budget deficit
Lower taxation on firms and lower interest rates

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements relating to the use of supply-side policy is correct?
options: Supply-side improvements in the economy can only be brought about by government policy.
Supply-side policies are intended to increase the long-run trend rate of economic growth.
Supply-side policies are designed to reduce the size of a negative output gap.
Supply-side policies ensure increased capacity utilisation in the economy.
